theorem.text: Does the formal statement say what the paper claims — no more, no less?
Could junk values (x / 0 = 0, default values, truncated subtraction) make the statement weaker than intended?
Are the edge cases (empty sets, zero, dimension 0 or 1) handled as in the paper?
Can all hypotheses be satisfied at the same time, or is the statement vacuous?
Are quantifiers, their order and the types of bound variables right?

definition.text: Does it define what the paper defines (and what its name suggests)?
Where the paper's definition does not apply (division by zero, outside the domain), does the value Lean assigns change any theorem that uses it?
Is it right at the edges: zero, empty sets, dimension 0 or 1, boundary points?
If it is a property: can it hold at all, and does it not hold trivially for everything?
Are the types right (ℕ, ℤ, ℝ, ℂ; which space), and the order of quantifiers inside it?

structure.text: Are these exactly the conditions (or data) of the paper — none missing, none added, none weakened?
Do junk values of the functions involved (x / 0 = 0, derivatives where there is no derivative) make a condition weaker than intended?
Are the edge cases handled as in the paper: t = 0, the boundary, dimension, closed or open intervals?
Can all conditions hold together, so that something satisfies the structure? Otherwise every theorem assuming it is vacuous.
Are quantifiers, their order and the types of the fields right?

purpose.theorem: This is the statement of a theorem. The Lean kernel has checked its proof; check that it states what the paper claims.
purpose.definition: This is a definition. Nothing is proven here: it fixes what a word means, and every theorem that uses it inherits any mistake. Check that it defines what the paper defines.
purpose.structure: This is a structure (a bundle of conditions or data). Nothing is proven here: theorems that assume it rely on exactly these conditions. Check that they are the conditions of the paper, no more and no fewer.

components.text:

  (∀ (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)),

        derivWithin (fun (x_1 : ℝ) => v x x_1) (Set.Ici 0) t +
            (fderiv ℝ (fun (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) => v x t) x) (v x t) =
          nu • Laplacian.laplacian (fun (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) => v x t) x -
              gradient (fun (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) => p x t) x +
            f x t) →
    (∀ (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)),
        ∀ t ≥ 0, NavierStokes.Comparator.divergence (fun (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) => v x t) x = 0) →
      (∀ (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), v x 0 = u₀ x) →
        ContDiffOn ℝ (↑⊤) (↿v) (Set.univ ×ˢ Set.Ici 0) →

source.title: Classical capacity and entropy inequalities for generalized amplitude damping (openai/math preprint)

paper.statement:
Let $\mathcal A_{\gamma,
u}$ be the generalized amplitude-damping channel, $\chi$ the Holevo information and $C$ the classical capacity, both in bits. For all $\gamma,
u\in[0,1]$ and every integer $n\ge1$, $\chi(\mathcal A_{\gamma,
u}^{\otimes n})=n\chi(\mathcal A_{\gamma,
u}) = rac n{\ln2}\max_{0\le p\le1}\{h((1-\gamma)p+\gamma
u)-g(v_{\gamma,
u}(p))\}$, where $v_{\gamma,
u}(p)=\gamma
u(1-
u)+\gamma(1-\gamma)(p-
u)^2$, $h$ is the binary entropy (natural logarithm) and $g(u)=h igl((1+\sqrt{1-4u})/2 igr)$. In particular $C(\mathcal A_{\gamma,
u})=\chi(\mathcal A_{\gamma,
u})$. If $p$ attains the maximum, independent products of the two equiprobable signals $\phi_\pm=\sqrt{1-p}\,|0angle\pm\sqrt p\,|1angle$ attain the Holevo information at every block length.

components.text:
{φ : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.Q3 ≃ OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.Q3} →
  (forward backward : ℝ × OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.CV → OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.CV) →
    (hamiltonian : ℝ × OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.CV → ℝ) →
      ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) forward →
        ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) backward →
          ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) hamiltonian →
            (forward_preserves :
                ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1,
                  ∀ (z : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.UnitQuadric),
                    OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.IsUnitQuadric (forward (t, ↑z))) →
              (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1,
                  ∀ (z : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.UnitQuadric),
                    OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.IsUnitQuadric (backward (t, ↑z))) →
                (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1,
                    ∀ (z : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.UnitQuadric) (a : ℂ),
                      Complex.normSq a = 1 → forward (t, a • ↑z) = a • forward (t, ↑z)) →
                  (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1,
                      ∀ (z : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.UnitQuadric) (a : ℂ),
                        Complex.normSq a = 1 → backward (t, a • ↑z) = a • backward (t, ↑z)) →
                    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1,
                        ∀ (z : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.UnitQuadric) (a : ℂ),
                          Complex.normSq a = 1 → hamiltonian (t, a • ↑z) = hamiltonian (t, ↑z)) →
                      (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1,
                          ∀ (z : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.UnitQuadric), backward (t, forward (t, ↑z)) = ↑z) →
                        (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1,
                            ∀ (z : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.UnitQuadric), forward (t, backward (t, ↑z)) = ↑z) →
                          (∀ (z : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.UnitQuadric), forward (0, ↑z) = ↑z) →
                            (∀ (z : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.UnitQuadric),
                                OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.project ⟨forward (1, ↑z), ⋯⟩ =
                                  φ (OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.project z)) →
                              (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1,
                                  ∀ (z : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.UnitQuadric) (v : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.CV),
                                    OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.Horizontal (forward (t, ↑z)) v →
                                      OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.omega (deriv (fun (s : ℝ) => forward (s, ↑z)) t) v =
                                        (fderiv ℝ (fun (w : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.CV) => hamiltonian (t, w))
                                            (forward (t, ↑z)))
                                          v) →
                                OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.HamiltonianPath φ

fun (φ : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.Q3 ≃ OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.Q3) =>
  ∃ (z : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.UnitQuadric) (v : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.CV),

          ∃ (U : Set OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.CV) (G : OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.CV → OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.CV),

paper.statement: Let $Q^3=\{[z_0:\dots:z_4]\in\mathbb{CP}^4: z_0^2+\dots+z_4^2=0\}$ with the restricted Fubini–Study symplectic form. There is a smooth Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\phi$ of this closed connected symplectic six-manifold with $\#\mathrm{Fix}(\phi)=3<4=\mathrm{Crit}(Q^3)=\mathrm{cuplength}(Q^3;\mathbb{Q})$. At least one fixed point of $\phi$ is degenerate.

paper.statement: Let $p,s,u,F,J$ be algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$, put $P=\mathbb{C}[p,s,u,F,J]$, $x=s^2+u^3+p^2F$, $H=x^2F-(1+2sx)J-p^2J^2-pu$ and $A=P/(H)$. Then $A$ is an integral complex algebra of dimension four, and for an independent variable $w$ one has $A[w]\cong\mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_5]$ but $A\not\cong\mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_4]$. Consequently the Zariski cancellation problem over the complex numbers has a negative answer in dimension four.

components.text:
∀ {L : ℕ → Type} {K : OAI.CHObstruction.ClassData L},
  (∀ {M N : OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel L}, K.strong M N → K.objects M ∧ K.objects N) →
    (∀ {M : OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel L}, K.objects M → K.strong M M) →
      (∀ {M N : OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel L}, K.strong M N → K.strong N M → M = N) →
        (∀ {M N P : OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel L}, K.strong M N → K.strong N P → K.strong M P) →
          ∀ (substructure : ∀ {M N : OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel L}, K.strong M N → M.IsSubstructure N),
            (∀ {M N : OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel L}, K.objects M → Nonempty (M.Iso N) → K.objects N) →
              (∀ {M N M' N' : OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel L} (h : K.strong M N) (e : M.Iso M') (f : N.Iso N'),
                  (∀ (x : ↥M.carrier), ↑(e.toEquiv x) = ↑(f.toEquiv ⟨↑x, ⋯⟩)) → K.strong M' N') →
                (∀ {M₀ M₁ M₂ : OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel L},
                    M₀.IsSubstructure M₁ → K.strong M₀ M₂ → K.strong M₁ M₂ → K.strong M₀ M₁) →
                  (∀ (γ : Ordinal.{u}),
                      γ ≠ 0 →
                        ∀ (F : γ.ToType → OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel L),
                          (∀ (i : γ.ToType), K.objects (F i)) →
                            (∀ (i j : γ.ToType), i ≤ j → K.strong (F i) (F j)) →
                              ∃ (U : OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel L),
                                K.objects U ∧
                                  OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel.IsUnion F U ∧
                                    (∀ (i : γ.ToType), K.strong (F i) U) ∧
                                      ∀ (N : OAI.CHObstruction.RelModel L),
                                        K.objects N → (∀ (i : γ.ToType), K.strong (F i) N) → K.strong U N) →
                    (∃ (θ : Cardinal.{u}), K.LSBound θ) → K.IsAEC

relies_on.doc: `Nonempty α` is a typeclass that says that `α` is not an empty type, that is, there exists an element in the type. Given `Nonempty α`, you can construct an element of `α` *nonconstructively* using `Classical.choice`.

source.title: A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold (openai/math preprint)

paper.statement: Assume the continuum hypothesis. There is an abstract elementary class $K$ in a countable finitary relational language such that (i) $\mathrm{LS}(K)=\aleph_0$; (ii) $K$ has at least two nonisomorphic models of cardinality $\beth_{\omega_2}=H(K)$, its Hanf number; (iii) with $\Lambda=\beth_{(2^{\aleph_1})^+}$, $K$ is categorical in every cardinal $\mu\ge\Lambda$. In particular $\lambda=\Lambda^+>H(K)$ is a categoricity cardinal from which downward transfer to $H(K)$ fails.

paper.statement: For every integer $r\ge4$ there is a constant $c_r>0$ such that every finite simple $K_r$-free graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and average degree $d\ge2$ satisfies $\alpha(G)\ge c_r\,n\log d/d$, where $\alpha(G)$ is the independence number of $G$.

source.title: An exponential state lower bound for two-way nondeterministic complementation (openai/math preprint)

paper.statement: For every integer $n\ge4$ put $H=\{1,\dots,n-2\}$ and let the alphabet $\Sigma_n=\mathcal R_H$ be the set of all binary relations on $H$. There is an $n$-state 2NFA $A_n$ recognising $L_H$ such that every 2NFA recognising $\Sigma_n^*\setminus L(A_n)$ has at least $\frac12\,2^{\lfloor(n-4)/127\rfloor}-1$ states. In particular there is no polynomial state bound for complementation that is independent of the finite alphabet.

source.title: Exact asymptotic moduli in a Daugavet subspace of L1 (openai/math preprint)

paper.locator: Introduction, main theorem (exact moduli), with the Kadets–Werner construction in the section on the construction
paper.statement: There is an infinite-dimensional closed real subspace $E\subseteq L^1$ (the Kadets–Werner construction) whose closed unit ball is totally bounded for convergence in measure and which has the slice property: for every $w\in S(E)$, every nonempty slice $\{y\in B(E):\ell(y)>\alpha\}$ and every $\rho>0$ there is a $y$ in the slice with $\|y\|=1$ and $\|w+y\|\ge2-\rho$; in particular $E$ has the Daugavet property. For every such space, every $x\in S_E$ and every $t>0$ satisfy $H_E(x,t)=\max\{t/2,t-1\}$ and $D_E(x,t)=\max\{0,t-2\}$. These are also the formulas for the moduli $\widehat\delta_E(t)$ and $\overline\delta_E(t)$, and $E$ admits no equivalent AUC norm.

paper.statement: For a positive integer $n$, $j(n)$ is the smallest positive $m$ such that every run of $m$ consecutive integers contains one coprime to $n$. With $\omega(n)$ the number of distinct prime divisors of $n$ ($\omega(1) = 0$), $h(k)$ is the supremum of $j(n)$ over all $n \ge 1$ with $\omega(n) \le k$. The start of the run is arbitrary.

questions.text: Does it define what the paper defines (and what its name suggests)?

Where the paper's definition does not apply (division by zero, outside the domain), does the value Lean assigns change any theorem that uses it? Here it relies on AddSubgroup, Complex, Fin, Nat, PreLp, ENNReal and 1 more: check what each of them means, and what it returns where the paper's notion is undefined.
Is it right at the edges: zero, empty sets, dimension 0 or 1, boundary points?
If it is a property: can it hold at all, and does it not hold trivially for everything?
Are the types right (ℕ, ℤ, ℝ, ℂ; which space), and the order of quantifiers inside it?

source.title: A Counterexample to the Group-Ring Determinant Conjecture (openai/math preprint)

paper.statement: There are a finitely generated discrete group $G$, an integer $n\ge1$ and a matrix $A\in M_n(\mathbb{Z}[G])$ that is invertible over $\mathbb{Q}[G]$ such that $0<\det_{\mathcal N(G)}(T_A)<1$. Here $T_A$ is the operator of $A$ on $\ell^2(G)^n$ and $\det_{\mathcal N(G)}$ the Fuglede–Kadison determinant; the logarithmic integral that defines it is finite and strictly negative. Thus the unrestricted group-ring Determinant Conjecture fails.

source.title: A Counterexample to the Group-Ring Determinant Conjecture (openai/math preprint)

paper.statement: There are a finitely generated discrete group $G$, an integer $n\ge1$ and a matrix $A\in M_n(\mathbb{Z}[G])$ that is invertible over $\mathbb{Q}[G]$ such that $0<\det_{\mathcal N(G)}(T_A)<1$. Here $T_A$ is the operator of $A$ on $\ell^2(G)^n$ and $\det_{\mathcal N(G)}$ the Fuglede–Kadison determinant; the logarithmic integral that defines it is finite and strictly negative. Thus the unrestricted group-ring Determinant Conjecture fails.

source.title: An exponential two-way deterministic state lower bound for one-way liveness (openai/math preprint)

paper.statement: For every integer $h\ge2$ the one-way liveness language $\mathrm{OWL}_h$ is recognised by a nondeterministic automaton with $h+3$ states using no left moves. Every equivalent deterministic two-way automaton with $s$ states satisfies $4(s+2)^2\ge2^{\lfloor(h-2)/31\rfloor}$. If an initially accepting configuration counts as acceptance, $s+2$ may be replaced by $s+1$.

paper.statement: For $n\ge2$, $2\le p<\infty$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is a constant $C_{n,p,\varepsilon}$ with $\|U(T)f\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^n\times I)}\le C_{n,p,\varepsilon} \|J^{s_+(p)+\varepsilon}f\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)}$, where $U(T)=e^{-iT|D|}$ is the half-wave propagator ($|D|=\sqrt{-\Delta}$), $I=[1,2]$, $J=(1-\Delta)^{1/2}$ and $s_+(p)=\max\{0,\frac{n-1}{2}-\frac np\}$. At $p=2$ one can take $\varepsilon=0$.

source.title: Entropy and Face Dimension of the Perfect-Matching Polytope (openai/math preprint)

paper.statement: Let $G$ be a loopless multigraph on $2m\ge2$ vertices with at least one perfect matching. For every $x$ in the perfect matching polytope $P(G)$, $F(x)-\left(2-\frac2m\right)B(x)\le H(x)\le F(x)$, where $H(x)$ is the largest entropy of a probability law on the perfect matchings of $G$ with edge marginals $x$, $F(x)=-\sum_e x_e\log x_e$ and $B(x)=-\sum_e(1-x_e)\log(1-x_e)$.

source.title: A Counterexample to the Infinite Matroid Packing/Covering Conjecture (openai/math preprint)

paper.statement: In ZFC there are a countably infinite set $E$ and two infinite matroids $M_0,M_1$ on $E$ with $M_i^*=M_i$ on the same labelled ground set ($i=0,1$) such that $I_0\cup I_1\ne E$ for every independent set $I_0$ of $M_0$ and every independent set $I_1$ of $M_1$. The pair $(M_0,M_1)$ has no packing/covering partition; consequently the infinite matroid packing/covering conjecture is false.

paper.statement: For all $a,b\ge1$ there are a positive integer $n$ and an origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ such that, with $L=[-1,1]^n$, $\log N(K,L)>b\log N(L^\circ,a^{-1}K^\circ)$. Here $N(A,B)$ is the least number of translates of $B$ that cover $A$ (translation vectors anywhere in the ambient space), and $^\circ$ denotes the polar body.

source.title: A product counterexample to the simplex maximum for projection-body volume (openai/math preprint)

paper.locator: Main theorem (counterexample), with equations (functional) and (proposed bound)
paper.statement: For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ let $R_d(K)=|\Pi K|/|K|^{d-1}$, where $\Pi K$ is the projection body of $K$; the simplex value is $c_d=(d+1)d^d/d!$, and the proposed simplex upper bound is $|\Pi K|\le c_d|K|^{d-1}$. With $T_{10}=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\dots,e_{10}) \subset\mathbb{R}^{10}$ and $K=T_{10}\times T_{10}\subset\mathbb{R}^{20}$, $R_{20}(K)/c_{20}=121\binom{20}{10}/(21\cdot2^{20})=22\,355\,476/22\,020\,096>1$, so $K$ violates the proposed bound in dimension twenty.

paper.locator: Introduction, theorem “Memory and precision”, with the definition “Finite-state Gaussian regression”
paper.statement: In the model of the paper a signal $s\in S^{d-1}$ is fixed before sampling; the learner reads, once and in order, $T$ pairs $(x_t,y_t)$ with independent $x_t\sim N(0,I_d)$ and $y_t=\langle x_t,s\rangle$, keeps a state from a set of at most $2^M$ elements, and outputs $\widehat s$. For every fixed finite $A>0$ there are constants $c_A>0$ and $d_A$ such that: if $d\ge d_A$, $M$ is an integer with $0\le M\le Ad^2$, $0<\epsilon\le1/10$, $S\sim\sigma_d$ is uniform on the sphere and independent of the rows and of the learner's data-independent randomness, and $\Pr\{\arccos\langle\widehat s,S\rangle\le\epsilon\}\ge2/3$, then the horizon satisfies $T\ge c_A\,d\log(1/\epsilon)$.

paper.statement: Take an $A$-by-$D$ rectangle with $AD=n$, row permutation group $R=(S_D)^A$ and column permutation group $C=(S_A)^D$. A pair $(r,c)$ is compatible if the row permutation $r$ followed by the column permutation $c$ can also be performed as a column permutation followed by a row permutation; $\mathcal I$ is this event and $U$ denotes independent uniform permutations in all lines. There are absolute constants $L,C_0>0$ such that: with $m=\sqrt n$, $m/2\le A,D\le2m$ and $m$ large enough that $\theta=1-L/\log m>0$, for all nonnegative functions $w_i:S_D\to[0,\infty)$ and $v_k:S_A\to[0,\infty)$, $\frac{n!}{|R||C|}\,\mathbb E_U[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal I}\prod_{i=1}^A w_i(r_i) \prod_{k=1}^D v_k(c_k)]\le e^{C_0n^{0.54}}\prod_{i=1}^A(\mathbb E\,w_i^{1/\theta})^\theta \prod_{k=1}^D(\mathbb E\,v_k^{1/\theta})^\theta$, the expectations on the right uniform on the symmetric groups and logarithms natural.
